solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Book lost by club member — clot

indicators.note: something lost by another word drops out of it, so this letter leaves the pieces

parts.note: taken as the word itself
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a fellow club member as an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A clump is a lump or mass, and a clot is a coagulated lump.

clue.text: Fellow accompanying prince is brought up as an orderly

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
Ras is an Ethiopian prince's title

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: taken as written before reversal

explanation.surface: A man escorting a royal is raised to be an attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaprassi is an Indian office messenger or attendant, an orderly.

clue.text: Sort of fringe an old pro cut from below

indicators.note: in a down entry read from below means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a moll is an old word for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A veteran working girl trims her fringe from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' shortens MOLL to MOL; A MOL read 'from below' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loma is a membranous flap or fringe, as on some birds' toes.

clue.text: Once celestial queen is found in the heart of such

indicators.note: is found in means the royal word sits inside the central letters
the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A heavenly queen is discovered at the centre of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as archaic; the 'queen' is Indian royalty rather than a monarch of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranic is an archaic word for heavenly, from Greek ouranos, the sky.

clue.text: Church layman tending the sick of old (as S. Paul on being upset about urchin)

definitions.text: Church layman tending the sick of old

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the urchin
being upset means these letters are overturned and rearranged

parts.note: an arab, or street arab, is a dated word for a street urchin

explanation.surface: An early Christian attendant of the sick is likened to a troubled saint around a street child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns S PAUL ON into P...OLANUS, wrapped 'about' ARAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Parabolani were lay helpers in the early Eastern church who nursed the sick at risk to themselves.

clue.text: Beat with American doodad

parts.note: to ding is to strike or beat

explanation.surface: A gadget gets hit with something from America.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingus is American slang for a gadget or thingummy.

clue.text: Bouncer from Johnson, erratic

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bouncer comes from the erratic Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' is not a doorman but a whopping lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is something outstanding, and a bouncer is a whopper or barefaced lie.

clue.text: Where Anthony lived and died, going into shell

indicators.note: going into means the letter for died goes inside the shell

parts.note: paua is a New Zealand abalone with an iridescent shell

explanation.surface: A saint's life and death drawn into a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Anthony of Padua lived and preached in this Italian city.

clue.text: Cork it's hell getting back, leaving aside opening

indicators.note: getting back means the trimmed word is read from its end to its start
the opening letter of the underworld's name is set aside and dropped

parts.note: Erebus is the dark underworld of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Someone finds getting back to Cork a hellish journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving aside opening' takes the first E from EREBUS, leaving REBUS; 'getting back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Suber is the botanical term for cork tissue, the bark of the cork oak.

clue.text: Is she unsettling to pure sisters if not TT?

definitions.text: Is she unsettling to pure sisters if not TT?

indicators.note: an unsettling act stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two letters of TT, here to be taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A nun asks if her drinking upsets her sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if not TT' signals that the teetotal letters are taken away before 'unsettling' does its work; a convent head may well unsettle her sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A superioress is a woman in charge of a convent, a mother superior.

clue.text: River suggesting the country separated from its source?

indicators.note: a word separated from its source loses its first letter

parts.note: rural means of the country

explanation.surface: A river hints at a land cut off from its spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' is the adjective rural, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from Russia through Kazakhstan to the Caspian.

clue.text: Climbing a hilltop, I planted a fig tree

indicators.note: planted means the single letter is set inside
climbing in a down clue means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a nab is a hilltop or projecting rock in northern dialect

explanation.surface: A hiker plants a fig tree on reaching a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns A NAB into BANA, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bania is a variant of banyan, the Indian fig tree.

clue.text: Plants denied light display it: see one riverain's holding up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards
holding means the riverain contains the number

parts.note: a Nilote is a Nile-dweller, and riverain means a riverside dweller
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A riverside dweller holds up a plant kept in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link; NILOTE 'holding' I, then 'up', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiolin is the yellow pigment in plants grown without light, which become etiolated.

clue.text: Dance music, the limit for harmonica?

definitions.meaning: a ring dance of Romania and Israel, and the music played for it
a fiendishly fast violin showpiece, ... Staccato, whose harmonica version is the ultimate test of a player

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition alludes to Dinicu's Hora Staccato, a virtuoso piece famously played on harmonica by Larry Adler.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a circle dance of Romanian and Jewish tradition and the tune accompanying it.

clue.text: A ruin, battered and corroded, rarely gilded

indicators.note: a battered thing is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
ate, as acid ate the metal

explanation.surface: An old ruin, beaten by weather and eaten away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges A RUIN into INAUR; 'rarely' warns that the word is seldom used.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaurate is a rare adjective meaning covered with gold, from Latin aurum.

clue.text: Like tea or coffee made for an audience?

indicators.note: something offered for an audience is heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: earned, as in made money

explanation.surface: A drink is prepared for an audience at a reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea or coffee served at gatherings comes from a large urn, so it is urn-dispensed.

clue.text: One muddled names and lives in recollection of Proust?

parts.note: an means one

indicators.note: muddled means these letters are jumbled

parts.note: is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: Someone muddles names and lives as Proust remembers things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges NAMES into AMNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Anamnesis is recollection; Proust's novel is a vast act of involuntary memory.

clue.text: Magic herb adding puff to a thin liquor, one gracing menu?

parts.note: to pant is to puff for breath
gruel is a thin watery porridge
I is the Roman numeral for one
a dish gracing the menu is on it

explanation.surface: A chef adds a magical herb to a thin broth so it can appear on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adding' is just a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelais's Pantagruel praises this marvellous herb, a comic name for hemp, so it is a fabled magic plant.

clue.text: Pillage of Scots creating touching condition

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A raid in Scotland leaves a moving situation behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Reif is a Scots word for robbery or plunder.

clue.text: Energy required in scrambling up tree, palm genus

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: scrambling mixes up these letters

explanation.surface: It takes energy to clamber up a palm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' rearranges UP TREE into UTERPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is a genus of tropical American palms, including the assai.

clue.text: Strong sweet wine sadly beak sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole run of letters is reversed

parts.note: alas expresses sorrow, sadly
a ram is the beak or projecting prow of a warship

explanation.surface: A magistrate returns a bottle of sweet wine, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' looks like the slang for a magistrate but is a ship's ram; 'sent back' reverses ALAS RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified dessert wine from Sicily.

clue.text: Rather angry about following asteroid

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: cross means angry, with -ish meaning rather

explanation.surface: An astronomer is a bit cross about pursuing an asteroid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asteroid' here is the old sense of a starfish, not a minor planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroid is the zoological term for a starfish, a star-shaped echinoderm such as a crossfish.

clue.text: Disgustingly posh, housed in e.g. mock ruin

indicators.note: housed in means the posh letter goes inside the building

parts.note: a folly is an ornamental building, often a sham ruin
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone posh is horribly lodged in a fake ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Foully means in a revolting, offensive way.

clue.text: Surrogate mother keeping son, so abandoned, in large shed

indicators.note: keeping means the surrogate holds the remaining letter

parts.note: Hagar bore Abraham's son for Sarah in Genesis

indicators.note: abandoned means the two letters of so are dropped from son

explanation.surface: A surrogate mother keeps her son in a big outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so abandoned' strips SO from SON, leaving N, which HAGAR is 'keeping'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangar is a large building for housing aircraft.

clue.text: Whisked lattes, hot — secret process

indicators.note: letters that are whisked are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A barista whips up hot lattes on the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whisked' rearranges LATTES into STEALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is furtive, covert action.

clue.text: Sort of Scottish punch — single drunk, not good

indicators.note: drunk means these letters are reeling about

explanation.surface: A single Scotch whisky punch, drunk and not good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes G from SINGLE before 'drunk' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An elsin is a Scottish awl, a tool for punching holes.

clue.text: Official adjudicators giving 'special' in ratings?

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the sailors

parts.note: tars are sailors, ratings in the navy

explanation.surface: Judges award special marks in league tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratings' are naval sailors, not scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar is an official appointed to direct policy in some field, a supremo.

clue.text: You'll find Trojan never imbibing such weakish spirits

indicators.note: you'll find signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Trojan warrior never drinks feeble liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' pretends to be drink; they are genies, and 'imbibing' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Jann are the lowest, least powerful order of jinn in Islamic lore.

clue.text: Fuss as cleaner is sacked? Confidence required

indicators.note: a sacked city is ransacked and turned upside down, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fussing over whether the cleaner gets fired takes nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' looks like dismissal but is the anagram signal for FUSS AS CLEANER.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assurance is confidence in oneself.

clue.text: Following difficulty striking new driver, golfer displays dejected air

indicators.note: striking means the learner's letter is struck out

parts.note: Nick Faldo, English golfer
L is the learner plate of a new driver

explanation.surface: After a miss with a new club, a golfer looks glum.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Following difficulty' also gives F and ADO, a second route to the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fado is a melancholy Portuguese folk song.

clue.text: Substantial piece of cake, second, shortened party

indicators.note: shortened means the party's name is cut down

parts.note: Labour is the UK political party

explanation.surface: A party offers a big slice of cake for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slab is a thick slice or piece, as of cake.

clue.text: Heads for courier in treating order with despatch

indicators.note: heads for means take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A courier deals with an order promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cito is Latin for quickly, used in prescriptions.

clue.text: It's certainly bordered by lines? Yes, or the other way round

definitions.text: It's certainly bordered by lines? Yes, or the other way round

indicators.note: one piece forms the borders of the other, which sits inside
the other way round means the affirmative word is turned backwards

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a passage really has lines along it, then flips the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other way round' both reverses YEA to AEY and swaps who borders whom, so the lines sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis alley is the strip between the singles and doubles sidelines, so it is bounded by painted markings.

clue.text: Dial up re being feverish, wanting relief from labour

indicators.note: feverish activity is agitated, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frantically phones about pain relief in childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being feverish' rearranges DIAL UP RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidural is an anaesthetic injected near the spine, widely used to ease childbirth.

clue.text: Monkey from South Africa with reverse of appeal

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

indicators.note: reverse of means the word for appeal is turned backwards

parts.note: it, as in sex appeal

explanation.surface: A monkey from South Africa has a backward charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The zati is the bonnet macaque of southern India.

clue.text: Thin fabrics — love coming into contact?

indicators.note: coming into means the nil score goes inside the other word

parts.note: a contact is a contact lens
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Lovers touch through filmy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contact' is short for contact lens.
explanation.definitionFit: Leno is a light open-weave cotton fabric, here plural.

clue.text: Rails over very long time cycle

indicators.note: over in a down sense, read in reverse, turns the birds' name backwards

parts.note: soras are North American rails, marsh birds

explanation.surface: A railway lasts over a very long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rails' are birds, not railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The saros is the eclipse cycle of about eighteen years.
